Thank you, Mr. President, for providing me with the floor to present the report of Committee 1, which I had the pleasure to chair. Distinguished delegates, ladies and gentlemen, Committee 1 first turned its attention to Workshop 1 on building resilient societies with a focus on protecting women, children, and youth, fostering engagement, education, and the culture of lawfulness. and met on the 26th and 27th of September in two sessions. Amongst the Chair's salient points taken from the workshop are the following. Many participants emphasized the importance of preventive strategies that address the root causes of crime by strengthening protective factors at the individual, family, and community levels. Discussions highlighted the value of data, research, and evaluation in designing evidence-based interventions by underscoring the need to move from consultations to co-creation by meaningfully involving women, children, young people, survivors, and persons with lived experience in the development of crime prevention and criminal justice policies and programs. Many participants also encouraged member states to invest in community engagement and resilience building measures that promote social cohesion, trust in institutions, and the culture of lawfulness in line with the Kyoto Declaration and the Abu Dhabi Declaration. We next turned our efforts to conducting workshop three on the 28th and 29th of September on getting ahead strengthening data collection and analysis to better protect people and planet in times of new, emerging, and evolving forms of crime. Amongst the Chair's salient points taken from this workshop are, many participants emphasized that high-quality, standardized, and interoperable data are essential for understanding and responding to new, emerging, and evolving forms of crime. including those that are increasingly transnational and technology-enabled. They highlighted the importance of strengthening data management, implementing international statistical standards, enhancing international cooperation and data sharing, and making better use of both traditional and non-traditional data sources to support timely, evidence-based, and people-centered crime prevention and criminal justice processes, responses. I am pleased to report that Committee 1 met yesterday, on 30 September, at 3 pm, to review and adopt the two reports which flow from these workshops, namely, first, workshop 1, entitled "Building resilient societies with a focus on protecting women, children and youth, fostering engagement, education and the culture of lawfulness"; And the second one on workshop three entitled Getting Ahead, Strengthening Data Collection and Analysis to Better Protect People and Planet in Times of New Emerging and Evolving Forms of Crime. As mentioned during the committee meetings, the report contains a procedural summary, whereas the rest of the report is a chair summary containing the elements of the discussions that I as chair consider to be the most relevant. These points were not negotiated by member states and simply reflect the points that I as chair wish to highlight. Together, these two reports constitute the whole report of committee one, which is now before the plenary for its consideration and eventual adoption. I should also like to take this opportunity to express my appreciation to all delegations, observers, and panelists for their valuable contributions to the work of the committee. I would also like to thank the two PNIs who co-organized workshops one and three, namely the United Nations Asia and Far East Institute for the Prevention of Crime and the Treatment of Offenders, UNAFE, and the Thailand Institute for Justice, TIG. Appreciation also goes to our UNODC focal points, Alexandra Martins and Tanya Wyatt, as well as Kayo Ishihara Kitti Boon Neohman, and Matti Joutsen, and Laetitia Ferhati, who all served as moderators for their respective workshops. Lastly, I would also like to thank the Vice Chair, Mr. Junichi Hashimoto, and the rapporteur, Mr. Carlos Sanchez, of the Committee, for their efforts in ensuring the successful conclusion of the Committee's work. Thank you.
